items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I told Billy Kyle Collins, and he laid on the floor laughing.

ctx.x: So he told me when he came out, he said, Trummy, you see all them pictures with the eyes and all coming out? He talking about modernistic paintings, you know. He said, did you see all those things? I said yeah. He said, what did you notice about them? I said, well, it's real modern, Louis, you know. He said, let me tell you something. You know who put those things up? I said no. He said, the Russians put them things out to confuse the Americans.

He said, if you see a horse, you know that's a horse, don't you? If you see a rose, you know -- I couldn't believe it, what he was talking. I told Billy Kyle Collins, and he laid on the floor laughing. I couldn't believe it. This guy -- laughed about two weeks until my stomach hurt me. I didn't know whether he was putting me on or whether he really, really believed it, but I couldn't believe it. I just couldn't -- these things -- he used to come on right out of the clear sky with, things like you just couldn't…

I couldn't believe things that he used to tell me, like funny, man. But, yeah, we go in Europe, and here's Princess Margaret and all of them like that, asking him about -- questions about things, and he's sitting up there having court with these big people.

Well, when I was in the Yacht Club, he was in the Downbeat. When I was in the Down -- he did go from club to club and the Downbeat later, but Dizzie never at and them were at the Onyx Club, and before Diz was in there John Kirby had a band in there. That was Billy Kyle on piano, Charlie Shavers on trumpet, Buster Bailey on clarinet, O'Neill Spencer on drums. He died years ago.

You know, everybody in that band is dead except Procope -- Russell Procope. He was on that band. That was a good band, very good band, and a lot of people used to go in there to hear them. They had a fantastic little group. Billy Kyle told me in fact that they rehearsed six months before they ever played a job. They rehearsed just -- they played different jobs, and they would get together and rehearse; you know, to make a living they all of them had different places they played, but he said they rehearsed about…
